title: Portugal Faces Twin Squeeze as Purchasing Power Falls and Public Debt Climbs · 25 Aug
keywords: Portugal, cost of living, purchasing power, public debt, inflation, fiscal policy, eurozone, European Union, budget, wages, Bank of Portugal, GDP, sovereign debt, European Commission
notes: Portuguese households are enduring their worst purchasing power in three years even as headline inflation moderates, creating a politically charged gap between official optimism and everyday financial reality. Meanwhile, public debt has risen to 92.9 percent of GDP in the second quarter of 2026, reviving a sharp debate over whether the government can maintain fiscal credibility while meeting citizens' expectations. The two pressures are closely linked: a state borrowing more than it planned has less room to cushion the very households already feeling squeezed.
